channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que governo Lula aumenta Bolsa Família por desespero
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the Lula government for increasing Bolsa Família by 15.04%, calling the measure an 'act of desperation'. The senator, PL presidential candidate, questioned the motivation behind the adjustment during public remarks.

item.title: Bolsonaro também ampliou benefícios em ano eleitoral; STF invalidou parte da medida em 2024
item.description: Lula announced a 15% increase in Auxílio Família in an election year, replicating Bolsonaro's strategy, whose similar raise was partially annulled by the Supreme Court in 2024.

item.title: Toledo: 'Datafolha mostra tendência de Flávio encostar em Lula'
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll indicates that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is narrowing the gap with Lula (PT) in the 2026 presidential race. Journalist José Roberto de Toledo evaluates the steady upward trend for Bolsonaro in the program A Hora da Pesquisa on Canal UOL.

item.title: Reajustar o Bolsa Família perto das eleições é ilegal? O que diz a lei
item.description: The Lula government announced a Bolsa Família adjustment outside the electoral period, which does not violate the law, but experts warn of risks of political power abuse. While the measure aims to reduce poverty, its proximity to the 2026 elections raises criticism about using public resources to influence voters.

item.title: Datafolha: 42% avaliam governo Lula como ruim/péssimo; 34% como ótimo/bom e 23%, regular
item.description: Datafolha survey shows 42% of Brazilians rate Lula's government as bad or very bad, 34% as good or very good, and 23% as regular. Negative ratings exceed positive ones by 8 percentage points.

item.title: Datafolha: No 1º turno, Lula tem 39% dos votos totais; Flávio, 36%; Cury, 6%; Caiado, 4%
item.description: Datafolha poll shows Lula leading with 39% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 36% in the first round. Cury and Caiado follow with 6% and 4% respectively.

item.title: TCU analisa política de preços da Petrobras na próxima 4ª feira
item.description: The TCU will hold an extraordinary session to analyze Petrobras pricing policy, including pricing criteria and governance. The meeting was convened by Minister Jhonathan de Jesus to oversee the Commercial Strategy adopted in 2023 and evaluate the new pricing model that considers international factors without automatic adjustments.

item.title: Mendonça rejeita ação no TSE que contestava reajuste do Bolsa Família
item.description: TSE minister André Mendonça rejected an electoral lawsuit filed by federal deputy Zé Trovão (PL-SC) challenging the 15.04% adjustment to the Bolsa Família benefit announced by President Lula. The decision was based on formal criteria, as the plaintiff and the president run in different electoral districts (state and national). The adjustment, raising the benefit floor from R$600 to R$691, takes effect in October starting on the 19th.

item.title: Bolsa Família: reajuste terá impacto de R$ 22,7 bilhões nas contas de 2027
item.description: The 15.04% adjustment to Bolsa Família, increasing the benefit from R$600 to R$691, will require the reallocation of R$22.7 billion in the 2027 budget, as stated by the Ministry of Planning. The government justifies the measure based on inflation correction and fraud prevention actions, but budget pressure may affect discretionary spending and social security.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 48% e desaprovado por 50%, diz Datafolha
item.description: A September 2026 Datafolba poll shows Lula with 48% approval and 50% disapproval, while 34% rate the administration "great" or "good", 23% "regular", and 42% "bad" or "poor". The poll, with a 2-point margin of error, was registered with the TSE and funded by Grupo Globo and Folha de S.Paulo.

item.title: Cinco pesquisas sobre o duelo Lula x Flávio em 2026 e qual mais acertou em 2022
item.description: Five recent polls show a balanced race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro for 2026, with three institutes favoring Lula and two favoring Flávio, all within the margin of error. In 2022, Paraná Pesquisas was the institute closest to the final result between Lula and Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Buscas por Bolsa Família disparam e diminuem desvantagem digital de Lula
item.description: The surge in Google searches for Bolsa Família, surpassing those related to the STF crisis, signals a strategic advantage for Lula's government, drawing attention to social issues in a digital landscape dominated by the right. August data shows increased interest in the benefit from the payment date, particularly in the North, Northeast, and Rio de Janeiro. This dynamic reduces the government's digital disadvantage and expands the digital battlefield.

item.title: Reajuste no Bolsa Família passa a valer em outubro; leia o que mudará
item.description: The federal government published Decree No. 13,120, adjusting Bolsa Família benefits by 15.04%, effective from October's payroll. The increase raises the average grant from R$777.00, with an additional cost of R$5.8 billion over the next three months. The measure was announced 17 days before the first round of elections and received a favorable opinion from the AGU stating there is no electoral prohibition.

item.title: Datafolha aponta empate triplo entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro; entenda
item.description: A Datafolha poll released two weeks before the first round shows a technical tie between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the presidential race, with 39% and 36% of voting intentions, respectively. Both candidates are also tied in rejection rates, each at 47%. In a simulated second round, Lula leads with 46% against Flávio's 44%, maintaining the technical tie.

item.title: Efeitos colaterais
item.description: Disclosures from PF investigations and the STF crisis directly influenced voting intentions for Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 elections, causing fluctuations in the gap between the candidates.

item.title: Datafolha: 50% desaprovam o governo Lula; aprovação é de 48%
item.description: A Datafolha survey released on September 17, 2026 reveals that 50% of voters disapprove of President Lula's government, while 48% approve. Direct government ratings show 42% negative (bad or terrible) and 34% positive (great or good), keeping the PT leader in a fragile position ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Holiday acusa Lula de crime eleitoral no Bolsa Família, mas vê suspensão como “tiro no pé”
item.description: Councilman Fernando Holiday (PL-SP) accused President Lula of electoral crime for raising Bolsa Família by 15.04%, but defended that the increase should not be suspended, calling it a 'foot shot'. He stated the measure will be challenged in Electoral Court.

item.title: Lula tem 46% contra 44% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha poll released on September 17, 2026 shows Lula at 46% versus Flávio Bolsonaro at 44% in a hypothetical second round, resulting in a technical tie within the ±2 percentage point margin of error. The survey, conducted between September 15 and 17, 2026, was registered with the TSE under number BR-04029/2026.

item.title: Mendonça extingue ação de Zé Trovão no TSE contra aumento no Bolsa Família
item.description: Minister André Mendonça dismissed the lawsuit filed by Congressman Zé Trovão (PL-SC) against the increase of the Auxílio-Brasil, citing lack of active legitimacy, as the candidacies belong to different electoral constituencies. Therefore, there was no analysis of Lula's proposal merits.

item.title: Cavalo assombrado
item.description: CartaCapital published a letter signed by Flávio Bolsonaro advocating for the legalization of civilian gun ownership, amid the 'Dark Horse' scandal and corruption investigations. The text aims to reinforce his image as a defender of gun rights, while facing pressure over alleged irregularities in funding negotiations for the biographical film about his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula pede responsabilidade na distribuição de canetas emagrecedoras
item.description: President Lula called for responsibility in the distribution of weight-loss pens through the SUS, warning against electoral misuse and advocating for medical guidance. During a visit to Eurofarma, he criticized mayors who might irresponsibly distribute medications, emphasizing the importance of dietary re-education. He also praised Minister of Health Alexandre Padilha and reaffirmed the government's commitment to free obesity treatment.

item.title: O duelo congelado entre Lula e Flávio no segundo turno, segundo o Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on September 17 shows stability in voter intent between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the second-round scenario, with 46% and 44% respectively, matching previous rounds. Despite fluctuations in the first round, the race between the two candidates remains technically tied for three weeks.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatam na rejeição, com 47% cada um
item.description: A Datafolha survey released on September 17 shows that Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are tied in rejection rates, both at 47%. The poll, commissioned by Globo and Folha de S.Paulo, surveyed 2,002 people between September 15 and 16, with a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

item.title: Datafolha: Lula tem 39% e Flávio, 36% no primeiro turno
item.description: Datafolha poll shows Lula (PT) at 39% and Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) at 36% in the first round, technically tied. Augusto Cury (Avante) holds 6% of voting intentions.

item.title: TRE-DF manda suspender propaganda de Michelle que usa imagem de Bolsonaro
item.description: The TRE-DF suspended campaign material from Michelle Bolsonaro featuring images of Jair Bolsonaro, following a lawsuit by Erika Kokay. The judge ruled that the combination of elements suggests support from the former president for the candidacy, contradicting STF rulings. The decision references a TSE precedent on restrictions regarding political imagery in campaigns.

item.title: Datafolha: Governo Lula é desaprovado por 50% e aprovado por 48%
item.description: The Datafolha survey released on September 17 shows that President Lula's (PT) government has 48% approval and 50% disapproval, maintaining statistics close to the previous survey. The administration's evaluation remains stable, with 42% considering it bad or terrible and 34% excellent or good, within the two percentage point margin of error. The survey was conducted between September 15 and 17 with 2,002 people aged 16 or older.

item.title: China defende eleições no Brasil e exalta relação entre Lula e Xi Jinping
item.description: The Chinese government defended Brazil's 2026 elections and highlighted the strong relationship between Presidents Xi Jinping and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The Chinese foreign ministry spokesman reaffirmed the principle of non-interference in internal affairs and criticized U.S. actions against Brazil. Beijing also praised Celso Amorim's recent visit to China, emphasizing the progress in strategic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Marinho diz que Lula transformou Bolsa Família em instrumento eleitoral
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), leader of the opposition in the Senate, criticized the 15.04% increase in Bolsa Família announced by President Lula's government (PT), accusing it of being used as an electoral tool. While acknowledging the program's importance, Marinho warned against its politicization, particularly given the proximity of upcoming elections.

item.title: Datafolha: Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula são rejeitados por 47% dos eleitores
item.description: Datafolha survey shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Lula are rejected by 47% of voters, reflecting extreme polarization in the Brazilian electorate. Both leading presidential campaigns are tied in rejection rates, indicating significant wear among the population.

item.title: Datafolha: Governo Lula tem avaliação negativa de 42% e positiva de 34%
item.description: A new Datafolha poll shows that 42% of Brazilians rate President Lula's government as bad or very bad, while 34% consider it great or good and 23% rate it as average. Released on September 17, 2026, the survey highlights a significant split in public opinion regarding the administration's performance.

item.title: Artistas apoiam reeleição de Lula e cobram mudanças na Cultura
item.description: Over 100 artists and intellectuals signed a manifesto supporting Lula's reelection, demanding changes in cultural policy and greater engagement from the Ministry of Culture. The document emphasizes the need for concrete cultural policies and sustainability for cultural professionals.

item.title: Zema, Renan e Caiado chamam de 'eleitoreiro' reajuste do Bolsa Família
item.description: Presidential candidates Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Renan Santos (Missão), and Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized the federal government's announced Bolsa Família readjustment, labeling the measure as electioneering.

item.title: Dólar fecha o dia em R$ 5,13 após decisões do Fed e do BC
item.description: The dollar closed at R$5.13 amid mixed pressure from the Fed and Copom, while the government announced an expansion of Bolsa Família. The Ibovespa rose 0.30% driven by Vale, despite volatility from the government announcement.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula participa de caminhada em Montes Claros
item.description: President Lula takes part in a walk in Montes Claros (MG) alongside Patrus Ananias, the PT candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, closing his schedule in the city. The event includes allies and candidates supported by the PT ticket in the state.

item.title: Ibovespa tem alta de 0,24% em meio a novas pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: The Ibovespa rose 0.24% to 185,900 points, driven by US and Brazilian interest rate decisions and the ongoing election race. Polls suggest Flávio Bolsonaro is gaining ground against Lula, according to a Veedha Investments analyst. The dollar fell to R$5.13 while banks showed mixed performance in the market.

item.title: Deputado Zé Trovão (PL), aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro, vai ao TSE contra aumento do Bolsa Família
item.description: Deputy Zé Trovão (PL-SC), an ally of Flávio Bolsonaro, asked the TSE to suspend a 15% Bolsa Família increase and fine Lula, arguing that it could benefit Lula's reelection campaign. The AGU defended the adjustment as legal and said it falls within the exceptions in Brazil's electoral legislation.

item.title: Por que esta eleição é a mais despolitizada e isso favorece a extrema direita
item.description: The article argues that the 2026 elections are the most depoliticized, with debates focused on corruption scandals rather than governance projects. This apathy favors the far-right, while the institutional left remains on the defensive, missing the opportunity to mobilize social policies that the right historically had to adopt to compete in contexts of inequality.

item.title: Publicitário ligado a Vorcaro estampa "adesivaço" de Flávio em carrão
item.description: Thiago Miranda, a publicist targeted by the Federal Police in investigations linked to Daniel Vorcaro and Banco Master, posted support for Flávio Bolsonaro on a luxury car and shared the senator’s campaign jingle. Police say Miranda also intermediated Vorcaro’s contact with Flávio in a film project about Jair Bolsonaro funded with resources under investigation and worked on communications defending the bank.

item.title: Há muitas diferenças entre o aumento do Bolsa Família de Lula e o de Bolsonaro
item.description: The report highlights that the Bolsa Família increase announced by Lula during an election period resembles Bolsonaro's 2022 measure, with both driven by electoral interests. Full content is subscriber-only.

item.title: Novo pede afastamento de Moraes do caso que apura mensagens com Vorcaro
item.description: The Novo Party requested STF President Edson Fachin to remove Justice Alexandre de Moraes from the case investigating messages with banker Daniel Vorcaro. The party argues Moraes acted as both an interested party and judge in the same proceeding, constituting a legal impediment.

item.title: Mendonça estava utilizando o cargo para fazer política, diz Lula
item.description: Lula accused Minister André Mendonça of using his role as rapporteur to conduct politics, citing alleged selective leaks tied to the Banco Master case. He also attacked Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro, suggesting the country needs transparency regarding process information. Lula defended simultaneous trials for all involved in the STF to prevent bias before elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vincula Lula a Moraes e diz que vai indicar 6 ministros do STF, caso eleito
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) linked Lula to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, claimed Lula owes him his mandate, and said he could appoint up to six STF ministers if elected. He favored conservative nominees and criticized the 15% increase in Bolsa Família as electoral desperation.

item.title: Governo Lula vê relatório sobre CV e PCC como manobra segura de Trump
item.description: The Lula administration views the U.S. accusation that it failed to confront the PCC and Comando Vermelho as a low-cost electoral move by Trump, less risky than sanctions against Supreme Court ministers. Although a significant share of Brazilian public opinion supports designating the groups as terrorist organizations, the government fears that renewed U.S. interference could benefit Lula.

item.title: Lula diz que não foca em pesquisas e critica Flávio: "Ligação com o Master"
item.description: Lula expresses confidence in his reelection bid and criticizes Flávio Bolsonaro over ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro, suspected of a banking fraud scheme. He highlights the recovery of R$ 6.5 billion from INSS and states he does not focus on polls, trusting that voters will decide on election day.

item.title: Bolsa Família: Lula repete Bolsonaro em medidas na véspera da eleição
item.description: Lula announces a 15.04% increase in Bolsa Família 17 days before the 2026 first round, raising the minimum benefit from R$600 to R$691. The measure, costing an estimated R$5.8 billion in 2026, mirrors the 2022 Auxílio Brasil expansion ahead of elections. The government claims inflation adjustment and states the measure complies with budgetary rules without extraordinary credit.

item.title: Lula acusa Mendonça de usar caso Master para “fazer política”
item.description: Lula criticizes Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça, accusing him of using the Banco Master case rapporteurship for political purposes. The president insists all involved must be judged and punished.

item.title: Governo Lula vê relatório sobre PCC e CV como 'muito grave' e brecha para ações militares dos Estados Unidos
item.description: Lula's government considers 'very serious' a US report accusing Brazil of failing to combat the PCC and CV factions, recently designated as terrorist organizations. Itamaraty fears the document could pave the way for US military actions, while the Ministry of Justice refutes the claims by highlighting the Anti-Gang Law and existing bilateral cooperation.

item.title: De interferência a crime organizado: o que Lula deve abordar na ONU
item.description: Lula will address the UN General Assembly and is expected to defend democracy, sovereignty and the integrity of Brazil’s electoral process without directly mentioning the United States. He will also address multilateralism, global conflicts, the environment, human rights and trade, while organized crime and the Supreme Court crisis are likely to take a back seat.

item.title: Lula endossou ato de Vieira de rejeitar exigências dos EUA sobre dissidentes, Boeing e terras raras
item.description: President Lula endorsed Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira's decision to reject a 21-point US proposal including demands for participation of political dissidents in 2026 elections and preferential access to critical minerals. The proposal was deemed unacceptable by Brazil's diplomatic corps and considered 'dead on arrival' after the minister reviewed its contents during meetings in Washington with Marco Rubio and US trade representatives.

item.title: Zé Trovão, aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro, vai ao TSE contra reajuste do Bolsa Família; Mendonça vai ser o relator
item.description: Congressman Zé Trovão, an ally of Flávio Bolsonaro, filed a lawsuit at the TSE against the Bolsa Família increase announced by Lula's government. The raise from R$ 600 to R$ 691 takes effect in October, amid the electoral calendar. The government and the AGU argue the measure only offsets inflation and is outside any electoral restrictions.
